name: Sleep on your back (anti-wrinkle)

lead: The idea is to sleep on your back so the face is not pressed into a pillow. It is claimed to prevent sleep lines.
Sleeping position is listed as a wrinkle factor, but no trial was found.

paras: Avoiding pressure and folding of facial skin during sleep.
Supine sleeping is associated with sleep apnea, reflux and sleep paralysis in some people.

forums.title: Fight Wrinkles and Sagging Skin: Top 5 Ingredients

lead: Sleeping on the back is promoted in appearance communities as a way to avoid 'sleep lines' and facial compression from pressing the face into a pillow. Proponents say side and stomach sleeping fold the skin night after night [1].

Encyclopedic sources list habitual sleeping position among factors contributing to skin wrinkles, alongside aging, sun damage and facial expressions, though the cited support is general educational material rather than a trial [1]. Back sleeping also has its own health associations, including more reflux and sleep apnea in some people [2].

paras: The practice involves sleeping supine, sometimes with a pillow arrangement to keep the face off the bed. Accounts of habitual sleeping position as a wrinkle factor are brief; the encyclopedia article on wrinkles names it once and points to a dermatology educational page [1].
Supine sleeping is linked to more positional obstructive sleep apnea, sleep paralysis and reflux when lying flat after eating, and side sleeping is the most common adult position [2].
No studies found comparing sleeping positions to wrinkle formation in the sources reviewed.

lore.intro: The tip appears in skincare and looksmaxxing discussion as a free anti-aging habit.

claims.claim: Side and stomach sleeping cause lasting sleep wrinkles.
